samasa.alt: कुल here has the sense ‘good family’, as in कुलीन. The compound may also be taken as a pañcamī-type bahuvrīhi, कुलजनेभ्यः प्रभवः यस्य; the sense is unchanged.

morph.note: सुकृतिन् is a possessive in -in from सुकृत ‘good deed’: ‘one who has good deeds’. Genitive plural -इनाम्.
धी ‘thought’ at the end of a compound declines as a root-noun: before a vowel ending ī becomes iy (कृतधियाम्).
Present participle of √अस् (सत्, the a of the root lost), genitive plural: ‘of those who are (truly)’, i.e. the good.
Imperative second singular of the curādi stem पालय-: the bare stem serves as the form. The hymn turns from description to request.

mantras.anvaya: या (त्वं) सुकृतिनां भवनेषु स्वयं श्रीः, पापात्मनां (भवनेषु) अलक्ष्मीः, कृतधियां हृदयेषु बुद्धिः, सतां श्रद्धा, कुलजनप्रभवस्य लज्जा (असि), तां त्वां (वयं) नताः स्म। देवि, विश्वं परिपालय।
mantras.anvaya_en: Five predicates in a relative clause (या … लज्जा, the verb ‘are’ understood), each with a genitive of the persons in whom she is that quality; the correlative ताम् त्वाम् is the object of bowing; a closing imperative.
mantras.lit: You who are yourself Śrī in the homes of the virtuous, Alakṣmī (in those) of the evil-souled, understanding in the hearts of those of cultivated mind, faith of the good, modesty of one born of a noble family — to that you we are bowed. O Devī, protect the universe.
mantras.tr: You are Fortune herself in the homes of the virtuous and Misfortune in the homes of the wicked; understanding in the hearts of the wise, faith in the good, modesty in the well-born. To you we bow: O Devī, protect the world.
mantras.tr_note: ‘Homes’ is supplied for the wicked from the first clause; ‘in the good’, ‘in the well-born’ render genitives.

comm.t: One Devī is named in five qualities, each placed in a kind of person: prosperity and its opposite, understanding, faith and modesty. The same power that blesses the virtuous is misfortune in the house of the wicked; the stanza does not make her two goddesses.

Several of these names return as forms of the Devī ‘established in all beings’ in the hymn of chapter 5: बुद्धिरूपेण (5.20-22), लज्जारूपेण (5.44-46), श्रद्धारूपेण (5.50-52), लक्ष्मीरूपेण (5.56-58). Brahmā’s hymn had already named her श्री and बुद्धि (1.79).
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) includes Lajjā among the Goddess’s names (name 740, लज्जा).
A modern reading: the stanza places the divine in a household’s fortune, a mind’s clarity, a person’s faith and restraint — the Goddess is met in character as much as in temples.

morph.note: Imperative first plural of the curādi stem वर्णय-: the first-person imperative (‘let us …’) with किम् asks a deliberative question — ‘how are we to describe?’
Neuter accusative singular of an -in stem: कारिन् → कारि (the n is dropped in the nominative/accusative neuter). It agrees with अतिवीर्यम्.
Gerundive (yat) of √चिन्त् ‘to think’ with the negative: ‘not to be thought’.

mantras.anvaya: (वयं) तव एतत् अचिन्त्यं रूपं किं वर्णयाम? असुरक्षयकारि भूरि अतिवीर्यं च किम्? देवि, सर्वेषु असुरदेवगणादिकेषु आहवेषु तव अद्भुतानि चरितानि च किम् (वर्णयाम)?
mantras.anvaya_en: Three questions with one verb (वर्णयाम), each introduced by किम्: the form, the valour, the deeds. The locative सर्वेषु … असुरदेवगणादिकेषु is taken as ‘among all the hosts’ (the battles fought among them).
mantras.lit: How should we describe this unthinkable form of yours? And (how) the abundant, surpassing valour that destroys the asuras? And (how), O Devī, your wondrous deeds in battles, among all the hosts of asuras, gods and the rest?
mantras.tr: How can we describe this form of yours, beyond all thought? Or your boundless valour that destroys the asuras? Or the wonders you have done in battle, O Devī, among all the hosts of gods, asuras and others?

comm.t: The gods confess that their praise cannot match its object: three questions, each beginning with किम्, about her form, her valour and her deeds. The hymn returns to the same three — form (रूप), valour (वीर्य) and conduct — in 4.21.
The confession of inadequacy is a convention of Sanskrit hymns, but here it follows directly on 4.4: if Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva cannot describe her power, the lesser gods can only wonder at it.
A modern reading: worship begins where description fails. The questions are not a refusal to speak but a way of speaking that keeps the mystery open.

flags.uncertain: The locative सर्वेषु … असुरदेवगणादिकेषु can be read ‘(in battles) among all the hosts of asuras, gods and others’ or, as a locative of reference, ‘(wondrous) to all the hosts …’. The first is followed here.

morph.note: Passive present of √ज्ञा: stem ज्ञाय- (ज्ञा + yak) with the ātmanepada ending -से, second singular: ‘you are known’. The agent of a passive is put in the instrumental, so दोषैः can be read as agent (see flags).
Past participle of वि + आ + √कृ (व्याकृत ‘separated out, made distinct’) with the negative अ-: the Sāṃkhya-Vedānta term for the undifferentiated cause before creation.
आद्य is आदि ‘beginning’ + the taddhita -य (the final i dropped): ‘being at the beginning, primal’; feminine आद्या.

mantras.anvaya: (त्वं) समस्तजगतां हेतुः (असि)। त्रिगुणा अपि दोषैः न ज्ञायसे। हरिहरादिभिः अपि अपारा (असि)। सर्वाश्रया (असि); इदम् अखिलं जगत् (तव) अंशभूतम्; त्वं हि आद्या परमा अव्याकृता प्रकृतिः (असि)।
mantras.anvaya_en: A string of predicates of an unexpressed त्वम्, one finite verb (ज्ञायसे, passive), a nominal clause about the world (जगत् अंशभूतम्), and the reason, introduced by हि: you are the primal Prakṛti.
mantras.lit: (You are) the cause of all the worlds; though possessed of the three guṇas, you are not known by faults; (you are) unfathomable even by Hari, Hara and the others; the support of all — this whole world is (your) portion; for you are the unmanifest, supreme, primal Prakṛti.
mantras.tr: You are the cause of all the worlds. Though you bear the three guṇas, no fault of theirs is found in you; even Viṣṇu, Śiva and the other gods cannot reach your farther shore. You are the support of all, and this whole world is but a portion of you, for you are the primal Prakṛti, supreme and unmanifest.
mantras.tr_note: ‘No fault of theirs is found in you’ follows the usual reading of दोषैः न ज्ञायसे (‘you are not known (to be touched) by faults’); see flags for the other.

comm.t: The hymn turns from her deeds to her nature: she is the cause of the worlds and the primal, unmanifest Prakṛti, of which the world is only a part. The paradox of the first line: she has the three guṇas, yet their faults do not cling to her. Even Hari and Hara do not reach her farther shore.

The vocabulary is Sāṃkhya (prakṛti, the three guṇas, avyākṛta), but the Prakṛti of this hymn is not an unconscious matter set against spirit: she is the Goddess herself, the cause and support of all. Brahmā’s hymn says the same (1.78: प्रकृतिस्त्वं च सर्वस्य गुणत्रयविभाविनी).
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) names the Goddess मूलप्रकृतिः (name 397) and त्रिगुणा (name 984) — the same two ideas in a different text.

flags.uncertain: दोषैः न ज्ञायसे admits two readings: ‘you are not known (to be touched) by faults’ (the usual one, followed in tr) or, with दोषैः as the agent of the passive, ‘you are not known by (those who have) faults’. Both are grammatical.
